name: The Kinks
hook: Two brothers, a slashed speaker cone, and the riff that taught rock guitar to sound broken on purpose.
blurb: Dave Davies cut slits in the speaker of a small cheap amp with a razor blade, which made the guitar sound fuzzy and mean. On 'You Really Got Me' in 1964 that sound was the whole record, and it is where hard rock's guitar tone starts. Distortion went from being a mistake to being the point. The Kinks matter twice over: Ray Davies' later songwriting invented the observant English storytelling that runs straight through Bowie, Blur and Pulp. The band were also banned from touring America for most of 1965 to 1969, which cut them out of the American market at exactly the moment their peers took it over.

signatureTracks.title: You Really Got Me
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The distorted riff as the entire architecture of a pop single.
